speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: There she lies. Green oak, near as yellow as a new deal, four bays, and pegged in the night or I am no cousin's friend. Twelve of you. I counted on the lane.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Poles to the two ropes. Heave when I say, and not when you feel brave. The first cross-frame only.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Keep her square. I am up here to see the pegs, not to admire a player's shoulders. Will, take the foot and let Richard have the thinking.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: The foot is mine and his. From the legs. Say nothing while she goes.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: From the legs.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Your twenty shillings is in her, Will. The timber. You are not buying the ale. The ale is my cousin's, after, and you need not stay to be praised for a shilling you have already spent.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not here to be praised. I am here to be one of the twelve.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Eleventh on this rope. The twelfth is the man at the brace. Heave.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Sweet. That is how a bay should go, as if it had meant to be in the air. Four of them. One done. Brace her before any of you tells a story.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Leave the stories. A frame that is up is a frame, and a frame that is talked of is still on the ground. The next is the long one.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Rest the hands. Not the mouths. Mouths have done enough.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She went up square. I'll say that once.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Say it once, then. Dull raises barns. We have two ropes and a yellow oak and the rest of the morning.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Water if you want it. The second rope is not a feast. Take the foot when I point, and wait for the word.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The next foot is yours with your brother. From the legs, the same as this one. I can see a shoulder from this ladder, and a shoulder is a poor pulley.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: From the legs, sir. The same.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: We'll see. Rest the hands until he points.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Two of the four are still on the ground. Do not spend the sweetness of the first on a speech about the second.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: The brace on the first is honest. Leave it. Poles back to the second rope.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Square again. By my troth, if she goes up as sweetly as her sister I shall have nothing to shout, and that would be a new experience.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I hope you are bored, sir.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Hope is a mouth. The foot is a foot. Take it when he says.

speaker: hamnet_sadler
text: Twelve at the start. I still count twelve. The ale is not a wage, and it is not yours to refuse yet, because you have not earned the refusing. Lift first.

speaker: (the carpenter)
text: Foot-men, to me. The long bay is the next word, and the word is not yet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'll wait for the word. Twelve still, and the first is already up.
